event: Weekly Market Review
title: Weekly Market Review
text:
BOTTOM LINE — Broad risk-off; AI hardware cracked, defensives and gas bid.
Semis led the unwind from Monday through Friday (SOXX -17.35% WTD), dragging the entire growth complex with it while staples and utilities held up. The tape fell apart into the close: every major index dropped 2-8% this week with the heaviest damage back-loaded into Friday's session. This was a de-risking of the AI thesis, not a rotation story.

INDICES — QQQ -10.51%, SPY -8.56%, DIA -8.04%, IWM -7.54% WTD. Small beat large by 1.90pp this week, but the magnitude was just as severe relative to a normal week. VIX at 28.4 versus a 20.9 20-day MA is a clear volatility spike — VIXY +13.42% Friday alone. Gold was the ugliest cross-asset move of the week (GLD -9.17% WTD), with silver collapsing alongside it (SLV -16.22%); USO gave back 17.64% over 20 days. Both SPY and QQQ closed below their 200-day moving averages.

SECTORS & ROTATION — Best to worst, WTD: XLP Consumer Staples -2.05%, XLU Utilities -3.07%, XLRE Real Estate -4.30%, XLV Health Care -6.15%, XLY Consumer Discretionary -6.27%, XLE Energy -6.85%, XLF Financials -7.00%, XLI Industrials -7.35%, XLB Materials -7.45%, XLC Communication Services -7.97%, XLK Technology -12.49%.
Industries top: UNG +4.04%, DBA -1.51%, KIE -2.42%, XLU -3.07%. Industries bottom: TAN -18.44%, SILJ -19.13%, DRAM -21.32%, WGMI -23.81%.
Money went out of energy (XLE -502mm) and financials (XLF -305mm) while staples quietly absorbed +53mm into XLB and XLK pulled in +580mm — a flight toward liquid index tech instead of sector bets. The week's state: AI hardware fading / high-to-low rotation.

DRIVERS — Semis and memory were the epicenter: SOXX -17.35% WTD, DRAM -21.32%, with NVDA -14.01%, MU -13.89%, and AMD -13.25% leading Friday's selloff. The Yahoo headline names Anthropic's IPO failing to revive the AI trade as the proximate narrative — but the move was already in motion by Thursday's 1,100-point Dow decline ahead of any single print. Internals confirm a broad unwind: breadth 122 up / 377 down, only 43 stocks above their 50-day, up/down volume ratio 0.20, and 138 new 60-day lows versus 2 highs. Defensives absorbed the exit — XLP finished green Friday (+0.67%) while everything cyclical bled. Consumer sentiment printed 51.5 (in line), and one-year inflation expectations cooled to 3.7 versus 4.30 prior — both consistent with a disinflationary pulse even as the tape panicked.

WHAT'S NEXT — VIXEQ at 57.9 (52-week top) and VVIX 127.1 signal extreme single-name dispersion; QQQ ATM implied vol at 53.1% and PCR 1.67 means options market is already leaning into further downside. SPY max-pain sits at 729 vs. spot near 7,175 (on the S&P cash print) — a gap to watch into Friday's monthly expiry. The Inflation Expectations print at 3.7 and Philadelphia Fed at 6.3 versus forecast 20 are conflicting inputs going into next week's S&P Global PMIs and Core PCE on 2026-11-25. FOMC is not until Dec 9 (Polymarket pricing 90% odds of a 25bp hike), so this week's move had no Fed catalyst behind it — which makes the rotation itself the signal, not a rate narrative.
